questions.questionHtml:
Let's make a trip to a new world called "Never Never Land".

Regular, ordinary first-order logic has two quantifiers: ∀∀ and ∃∃.

Now, let's imagine we lived in a world in which these quantifiers didn't exist, and instead we only had one quantifier, NN. The quantifier NN is the "never" quantifier, and the expression
Nx.[some formula]Nx.[some formula]
means "[some formula] is never true, regardless of what choice of xx we pick." For example, the expression
Nx(P(x))Nx(P(x)) says "There is No element xx in the domain, such that P(x)P(x) is true".

For predicates A(x)A(x) and B(x)B(x), Which of the following is the correct expression for “All A's are B's" ?“All A's are B's" ?
